wec.title: Windows integration (Event Forwarding)
wec.intro: Windows servers send their events agentlessly via Windows Event Forwarding (Kerberos, port 5985) to the appliance. Setup takes three steps.
wec.step1: 1. Define domain, appliance FQDN and target groups

roles_hint.dc: Security, Directory Service, DNS, System – one OU (distinguished name) per line.
roles_hint.member: Logons, processes, services, tasks, file access, PowerShell, Defender.
roles_hint.client: Lean selection: failed logons, local admins, Defender, services, USB.

wec.step2_text: Run the script as a domain administrator on a domain controller (with RSAT). It creates the service account, SPN, keytab and one GPO per role and links them to the OUs.
wec.step3_text: Upload the file siem-wec.keytab created by the script (principal {{principal}}), then delete it on the domain controller.
wec.check_text: Checks whether servers really apply the recommended audit policy (e.g. if the GPO is not applied yet). Run the script on a DC or via remoting for several servers – it changes nothing – and upload the generated JSON file here.
wec.audit_text: The GPO applies this advanced audit policy on all target systems.

linux.title: Connect Linux servers
linux.intro: Agentless via rsyslog (syslog over TLS, port 6514) with optional auditd rules. Supports Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL family and SUSE.
linux.server: Appliance address (as seen from the servers)
linux.server_hint: Hostname or IP the Linux servers can reach; port 6514 must be allowed in the firewall for these servers.
linux.audit: Set up auditd rules (users, sudo, SSH, configuration files)
linux.step2_text: Run as root. The script installs rsyslog with the TLS module, stores the CA certificate, sets up forwarding and sends a test message. Then add the server under Devices with type “Linux server” or wait for auto-detection.

sophos.title: Connect Sophos Central
sophos.intro: Events and alerts from Sophos Central. Primarily via the XDR Data Lake; without a license automatically via the SIEM integration API. Polled every 10 minutes. Create API credentials (client ID/secret) in Sophos Central under “Global Settings → API Credentials” with the role “Service Principal Read-Only”.

sophos.probe_siem: Connection ok – no Data Lake, SIEM API will be used.
